newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir crew opens freighter hatch, to start unloading.
newsitem.headline: Mir crew opens freighter hatch, to start unloading.

text.p: Cosmonauts on board Russia's Mir space station opened the hatch leading to a docked supply ship on Tuesday and are ready to start unloading tools crucial for the troubled mission, a senior flight official said.
The unmanned Progress craft contains oxygen, food, water and tools needed for repairs to the Spektr module, badly damaged on June 25 when another supply ship hit the ageing space station.

"They opened the hatch and will be unloading soon," Viktor Blagov, deputy flight director, told Reuters, adding that the operation would take three days to complete. "Unloading is a routine operation and everything is proceeding normally."

The cargo ship successfully docked with Mir on Monday, but unloading had been postponed because of the need to recharge the batteries of the Kvant module where Progress is attached. Mir lost up to half its electric power in the June 25 collision.
Also aboard the Progress craft are parcels from the families of the three-man Russian-U.S. crew and personal belongings for American astronaut Michael Foale, who lost his in the accident.
Vladimir Solovyov, the flight director, said the crew would first unload personal belongings, then repair tools and scientific research equipment.
"Foale has returned to his biological experiments under a NASA programme," Solovyov said. The crew had to stop all scientific work after the accident.

Foale's two Russian cosmonaut colleagues, Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin, will enter the Spektr in heavy spacesuits to repair the power supply, probably around July 18, although no final date has been fixed.
During Mission Control's communication with the crew on Monday a senior doctor, Igor Goncharov, urged them to avoid exerting themselves too much during the unloading of Progress.
He also advised them to get plenty of rest and to take lots of vitamins in the coming days as they prepare for their sortie to the holed module to reconnect electrical cables.

Space officials said on Monday the cosmonauts may not have to fully enter the module to do repairs, but could do the work half inside Spektr and half in the hatch. Foale will sit in the Soyuz escape capsule for safety during the repair work, which is expected to last up to four hours.
